name: Pantheon (church of Sainte-Genevieve)
aka: Ancienne église Sainte-Geneviève, devenue Le Panthéon

dates.built: 1755-1780 (the span of the campaign years the Mérimée notice prints)
dates.altered: The Mérimée notice records that the church 'a été transfomée en monument commémoratif pendant la Révolution', was returned to worship under the Restoration and became a commemorative building again during the nineteenth century; it names Quatremère de Quincy, who walled up the windows.
dates.note: THE REGISTER'S CAMPAIGN YEARS DO NOT MATCH THE NODE'S DATES. The node's exemplar says 'foundations 1758, completed 1790 by Rondelet'; the Mérimée notice prints 'Année(s) de(s) campagne(s) de construction 1755 ; 1764 ; 1780' and dates the principal campaign '2e moitié 18e siècle'. fr.wikipedia's infobox prints 'Construction 1757-1790 (projet : 1744)' and 'Hauteur 84 m'. Three sources, three sets of years; none is changed here.

quotes.text: L'église Saint-Geneviève, édifiée par Soufflot dans la seconde moitié du 18e siècle, a été transfomée en monument commémoratif pendant la Révolution. Elle est rendue au culte sous la Restauration, mais redevient édifice commémoratif dans le courant du 19e siècle.

measurements.note: A year, not a dimension, and three years earlier than the 1758 the node's exemplar gives for the foundations. `count` is the nearest unit the closed enum offers.

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. The pivotal building of this node's own argument - 'Soufflot's Sainte-Genevieve is the pivotal object because it takes the structural ambition of Gothic ... and executes it in a wholly classical vocabulary, using iron cramps hidden inside the piers' - and the register says nothing about any of it: no material, no order, no pier dimension, no iron. It records the building's changes of USE, which is what a protection notice is for. The 84 m height is on fr.wikipedia only and is therefore not carried as a measurement. No rights line was read, so no `rights_evidence`.
